standard: All requested material parts, independently per answer. Grade the ruling, not support labels.

grades.question: How does each player prepare their ID and Voting cards, what happens to cards for unused colors, and how is the initial Gold Bar pool dealt?
grades.expected_answer: Stand a visible ID in your chosen color, take the matching Voting set, remove target cards for colors not playing, and retain your Ambush card. Put the Gold deck face down and deal four central Gold Bar cards with values hidden.
grades.observed_answer: Each player puts their Player ID card upright in its plastic stand, visibly in front of them. Give each player the Voting card set with that player's color on its backs; remove cards targeting colors not playing and keep the player's own Ambush. Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center, keeping their values hidden.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup: “upright in their plastic stand”; “Remove cards targeting colors that are not playing”; “Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center.”
grades.reason: Explicit upright stand and visible chosen-color ID, matching Voting cards, unused colors removed, own Ambush retained and hidden central4 deal.

grades.question: Is there a player-by-player voting turn order? When may a player change their face-down choice, and when are choices revealed?
grades.expected_answer: There is no turn order. Choices can change until reveal. Once everyone has chosen, all reveal simultaneously.
grades.observed_answer: There is no player-by-player turn order. A player may change their face-down card until cards are revealed; once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
grades.reader_evidence: “There is no individual turn order”; “You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed”; “reveal all choices simultaneously.”
grades.reason: Explicitly states no player turn order, changes until reveal, and simultaneous reveal after all have chosen.

grades.question: In a seven-player vote, Red receives three votes, Blue two and Green two. Is a four-vote majority necessary to make Red a Target? Explain the Target threshold.
grades.expected_answer: No majority is required: the greatest vote total determines the Target. Red alone is Target because three is the highest count.
grades.observed_answer: No four-vote majority is needed. The Target is the player receiving the most votes; with 3 votes against Red and 2 each against Blue and Green, Red alone is the Target.
grades.reader_evidence: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target.”
grades.reason: Applies highest count rather than absolute majority: Red alone is Target at three versus two and two.

grades.question: Red and Blue tie for the most votes. With neither playing Ambush, what happens to them, and may someone survive by having voted for either tied Target?
grades.expected_answer: Both tied Targets are eliminated. A non-Target voter who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and is not eliminated for voting outside the Target group.
grades.observed_answer: Both tied players are Targets. Neither is protected by Ambush in this scenario, so both are eliminated. A player who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and may survive, subject to the successful Ambush exception.
grades.reader_evidence: “If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets”; “With tied Targets, voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.”
grades.reason: Both tied Targets eliminated absent successful Ambush; vote for either Target satisfies the survival voting requirement.

grades.question: Blue is the sole Target. Green received no votes and voted for Red. Green did not Ambush. Does receiving no votes keep Green alive?
grades.expected_answer: No. A player who did not vote for a Target is also eliminated, even when nobody voted for that player. Green voted outside the Target group and is eliminated.
grades.observed_answer: No. Green is eliminated because Green did not vote for the Target, Blue. Receiving no votes does not keep Green alive.
grades.reader_evidence: “Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated.”
grades.reason: Green is eliminated for voting outside the Target group despite receiving no votes.

grades.question: Red plays Ambush, Yellow votes for Red, and Pink votes for Yellow. How are votes tallied, who are the Targets, and who survives after Red's legal retaliation?
grades.expected_answer: Ambush adds no vote. Red and Yellow each have one vote and are tied Targets. Yellow is eliminated; Red survives its successful Ambush and can retaliate only against Yellow, who voted for Red. Pink voted for tied Target Yellow and survives, leaving Red and Pink.
grades.observed_answer: Ambush cards do not count as votes. Yellow's vote for Red and Pink's vote for Yellow each count, producing a one-vote tie between Red and Yellow; both are Targets. Red's Ambush succeeds, so Red survives and may eliminate Yellow, the player who voted for Red. Pink survives because Pink voted for a tied Target, Yellow. Red and Pink remain.
grades.reader_evidence: Illustration: “Red plays Ambush, Yellow votes for Red, and Pink votes for Yellow. Red and Yellow tie at one vote each and are both Targets. Yellow is eliminated; Red survives ... Pink ... survives, leaving Red and Pink.”
grades.reason: Complete vote tally ignoring Ambush, Red/Yellow tied Targets, Red protected/retaliates on Yellow, and Pink survives for voting TargetYellow.

grades.question: A Target successfully plays Ambush and four players voted for them. Do they eliminate all four voters? May they choose a player who voted for another color instead?
grades.expected_answer: The ambusher survives and eliminates exactly one of the players who voted for them. They neither eliminate every voter nor choose someone who did not vote for them.
grades.observed_answer: No. The successful ambusher chooses only one player who voted for them, even if four players did so. They may not choose someone who voted for another color instead.
grades.reader_evidence: “chooses one of the players who voted for them”; “cannot choose ... someone who voted for a different Target.”
grades.reason: Restricts successful Ambush retaliation to exactly one voter who targeted the ambusher; rejects all-voter and arbitrary-color alternatives.

grades.question: A player chooses Ambush but is not among the Targets after the votes are counted. What happens to that player?
grades.expected_answer: The Ambush fails and that player eliminates themselves.
grades.observed_answer: The player eliminates themselves. An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails.
grades.reader_evidence: “An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.”
grades.reason: Non-Target Ambush fails and self-eliminates.

grades.question: Four players survive a vote and its Ambush effects. Does the round award gold now, and who participates next?
grades.expected_answer: The round continues with another conspiracy and vote among the four survivors. It ends when the resolved vote leaves one, two or no survivors.
grades.observed_answer: No gold is awarded yet. Since four survive, they continue with another conspiracy and vote, and only those surviving players participate in the subsequent vote.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: “Three or more | Continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.”
grades.reason: Four survivors continue conspiracy/voting; no gold yet and only survivors vote.

grades.question: Exactly one player survives the round. What reward do they collect, and are the four cards four points?
grades.expected_answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. Four bars are four cards, not four points; each Gold Bar is worth 3, 4 or 5 points.
grades.observed_answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are four cards, not four points; each card has a value of 3, 4, or 5 points.
grades.reader_evidence: “That survivor collects all four central Gold Bars”; “receiving one bar means receiving one card whose value is 3, 4, or 5 points.”
grades.reason: Sole survivor takes all four central cards; explicitly distinguishes cards from 3/4/5 point values.

grades.question: Exactly two players survive the voting. What must they do, which cards does each receive, and how do they choose and reveal?
grades.expected_answer: They must hold a Final Showdown. Each receives Share, Steal and Grab One & Go, may discuss intentions, secretly chooses one card face down, and reveals simultaneously with the other finalist.
grades.observed_answer: They resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set of Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go cards, may discuss intentions and a bargain, then each chooses one card face down. When both are ready, they reveal simultaneously.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown: each “takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go”; each chooses one face down; “reveal both choices simultaneously.”
grades.reason: Explicit Share/Steal/Grab One & Go set, discussion, secret face-down selection and simultaneous reveal.

grades.question: The final vote eliminates every participant. Who receives gold from the deck, who does not, and what happens to the four central bars for next round?
grades.expected_answer: Nobody receives the central bars. Every player not involved in that final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck; participants in that final vote receive none. Leave the four central bars and add no new central gold next round.
grades.observed_answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck; the players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar for this outcome, including those eliminated by it. Nobody collects the four central bars. Leave those four bars for the next round and add no new bars.
grades.reader_evidence: No survivors: “Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave the four central bars for the next round; add no new bars.”
grades.reason: Rewards only those absent from the final vote one deck card each; final voters receive none; all four central cards retained with no additions.

grades.question: Both finalists reveal Share. How many Gold Bar cards does each receive?
grades.expected_answer: Each finalist receives two of the four central Gold Bar cards.
grades.observed_answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table, Share vs Share: “You get 2; opponent gets 2.”
grades.reason: Share/Share yields two central cards each.

grades.question: One finalist reveals Share and the other Steal. How are the central Gold Bars divided?
grades.expected_answer: The Share player receives no bars and the Steal player receives all four.
grades.observed_answer: The player choosing Share receives zero bars; the player choosing Steal receives all four central bars.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table, Share vs Steal: “You get 0; opponent gets 4.”
grades.reason: Steal takes all four, Share takes zero.

grades.question: One finalist reveals Grab One & Go and the other Steal. How are the central Gold Bars divided?
grades.expected_answer: Grab One & Go receives one bar and Steal receives three.
grades.observed_answer: The player choosing Grab One & Go receives one bar, and the player choosing Steal receives the other three bars.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table, Steal vs Grab One & Go: “You get 3; opponent gets 1”; “Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.”
grades.reason: Grab One & Go takes one and Steal three.

grades.question: One finalist reveals Grab One & Go and the other Share. How are the central Gold Bars divided?
grades.expected_answer: Grab One & Go receives one bar and Share receives three.
grades.observed_answer: The player choosing Grab One & Go receives one bar, and the player choosing Share receives the other three bars.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table, Share vs Grab One & Go: “You get 3; opponent gets 1”; Grab One & Go “gives its player exactly one bar.”
grades.reason: Grab One & Go takes one and Share three.

grades.question: Both finalists reveal Grab One & Go. How many bars does each take, how many remain central, and how many new central bars are dealt if play continues?
grades.expected_answer: Each takes one central bar. Leave the other two central and deal just two new central bars for the next round.
grades.observed_answer: Each takes one central bar; two remain in the center. If play continues, add just two new bars for the next round.
grades.reader_evidence: “If both choose Grab One & Go, each finalist receives one central bar. Leave the remaining two in the center and add just two new bars for the next round.”
grades.reason: Each takes one; two remain and only two new central cards dealt if continuing.

grades.question: Both finalists reveal Steal. What do the finalists and the other players receive, and what happens to the central pot?
grades.expected_answer: Both finalists receive nothing. Each other player receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round rather than replacing them.
grades.observed_answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
grades.reader_evidence: “If both choose Steal, neither finalist receives gold”; “give every other player one Gold Bar from the deck”; “Leave all four central bars for the next round.”
grades.reason: Finalists get zero, every other player one deck card; all four central cards retained without additions.

grades.question: When is victory checked, what totals win with 6–9 versus 10–12 players, and who wins if multiple players qualify with different totals?
grades.expected_answer: Check at round end after Gold Bar awards. The threshold is 25 points with 6–9 players and 24 with 10–12. When several qualify, the highest total wins.
grades.observed_answer: Victory is checked at the end of a round, after Gold Bars are awarded, regardless of how the round ended. With 6–9 players, the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12, at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the highest point total wins.
grades.reader_evidence: “Check for victory at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded”; thresholds “at least 25” and “at least 24”; “the highest point total wins.”
grades.reason: Checks after awards at round end for every outcome; gives 25 for6–9,24 for10–12 and highest qualified total wins.

grades.question: At game end exactly two qualifying players tie for the highest Gold point total. What does the booklet require? If a normal round ends without a winner, which eliminated players return?
grades.expected_answer: The tied players conduct another Final Showdown, repeating until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. If no winner ends the game, every player returns next round: stand all IDs upright again.
grades.observed_answer: The booklet requires tied leaders to conduct another Final Showdown, repeating as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total. It does not end the tie after one extra Showdown if the highest totals remain tied. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns, including players eliminated earlier in the round; stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.
grades.reader_evidence: “Repeat these Showdowns as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total”; “If there is no winner, everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright.”
grades.reason: Exactly two tied qualified highest players hold further Showdowns until a single highest player exists; all players return with IDs upright if normal play continues.

grades.question: Before each vote, about how long should conspiracy last, may players communicate secretly or by texting/showing cards, and who asks for final decisions when it is time to vote?
grades.expected_answer: Conspire for no longer than roughly a minute and a half. Any overt or covert means is allowed, including texting and showing Voting cards. The game owner asks players for their final decisions before voting.
grades.observed_answer: Before every vote, players discuss or signal intended targets for roughly a minute and a half at most. Any communication method is allowed, including secretly, texting, or showing a Voting card. When it is time to vote, the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.
grades.reader_evidence: Conspire: “for roughly a minute and a half at most”; “speaking, whispering, gestures, showing a Voting card, texting”; “the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.”
grades.reason: Gives approximate90-second maximum before each vote, any overt/covert communication including requested examples, and game-owner final-decision call.

grades.question: When casting an ordinary vote rather than Ambush, which card do you choose and where do you put it? What card replaces that choice if you suspect you are the Target?
grades.expected_answer: Choose the Voting card matching the ID color of the person you want to eliminate and place it face down in front of you. Play your own Ambush card instead of choosing another player’s card if you suspect you are the Target.
grades.observed_answer: For an ordinary vote, choose the Voting card matching the color of the player's visible ID you want to target, and place it face down. If you suspect you are the Target and want to defend yourself, play your own Ambush card instead.
grades.reader_evidence: “To target someone, use the card matching that player's visible ID color”; “Each surviving player places one Voting card face down”; “play your Ambush card instead.”
grades.reason: Target-color card, face-down orientation and Ambush substitution supplied, but location in front of the voter omitted. This requested location is also omitted from the summary’s Vote prose; sourcep5 specifies it.

grades.question: After resolving a vote, how do the Player ID cards show who has been eliminated and who is eligible for the next vote?
grades.expected_answer: Knock over eliminated players’ IDs. Surviving IDs stay standing; only survivors participate in the next vote.
grades.observed_answer: Knock down the ID cards of eliminated players. Leave survivors' IDs upright; those surviving players are eligible for the next vote.
grades.reader_evidence: “Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving IDs upright for the next vote.”
grades.reason: Knocks eliminated IDs down and leaves survivors upright/eligible for next vote.

grades.question: A round awards all four central bars, either to a sole survivor or through a Showdown that distributes the entire pot. If nobody wins the game, how is the next central pool prepared?
grades.expected_answer: Deal four new central Gold Bar cards for the next round, keeping their values hidden. Refill to four only if play continues; the retained-pot exceptions apply when bars were left behind.
grades.observed_answer: After the round, if nobody has won, everyone returns. Keep any central bars left behind and refill the central pool to four bars as needed; bars explicitly left behind remain there.
grades.reader_evidence: “Refill the central pool to four Gold Bars as needed; bars explicitly left behind remain there.”
grades.reason: Refill-to4 resolves four new cards after full distribution (readerB makes number explicit). Both omit hidden-value/face-down preparation of the new pot. Independent adjudication confirms partial for that requested preparation detail.

grades.question: In the illustrated vote with four votes for Blue and three for Purple, Blue plays a successful Ambush. Does Purple become the Target because Blue survives, and may voters for Purple survive on that basis?
grades.expected_answer: No. Blue remains the Target from the tally, even though Ambush protects Blue. Purple is not promoted to Target; players who did not vote for Blue are eliminated. Blue also chooses one player who voted for Blue to eliminate.
grades.observed_answer: No. Blue remains the only Target because Blue has the most votes; Blue's successful Ambush protects Blue but does not make Purple a Target. Voters for Purple have not voted for a Target, so they are eliminated under the voting requirement, unless individually protected by a successful Ambush.
grades.reader_evidence: The summary does not describe this four-vote/three-vote example. It states: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target”; Ambush “does not ... prevent another player from being a tied Target”; and players who “did not vote for any Target” are eliminated.
grades.reason: Correct fixed TargetBlue after tally and successful protection; Purple not promoted and Purple voters eliminated. Generic Ambush caveat cannot apply to ordinary Purple voters and changes no actual ruling. Blue-voter retaliation is extra key context, not requested. Independent adjudication agrees.

grades.question: Three qualifying players are tied for the highest total at game end. What tie instruction does the booklet give, and does it specify how to arrange a Final Showdown among more than two players?
grades.expected_answer: The tied players must conduct another Final Showdown until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. The booklet provides only a two-player Showdown procedure and no arrangement for three or more tied players. A specific multiway procedure is unresolved in this source; do not invent one.
grades.observed_answer: The instruction is for tied leaders to conduct a Final Showdown and repeat Showdowns as necessary until one player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total. The summary says the booklet does not specify how to arrange a Final Showdown among more than two tied players; its procedure and payoff table cover only two players, so the three-player arrangement is unspecified.
grades.reader_evidence: “the booklet directs tied leaders to a Final Showdown”; “covers only two players. It provides no arrangement for three or more players tied.”
grades.reason: Accurately gives repeated Showdown requirement and explicitly identifies absence of a three-or-more-player arrangement; answers source-limitation question completely without inventing a solution.

grades.question: During an extra Final Showdown between two players tied for the qualifying highest total, both Steal. Could a player outside that pair become the winner if the compensation bar gives that player the single highest total?
grades.expected_answer: Yes. Double Steal gives every player outside the pair one Gold Bar from the deck while the finalists get nothing. The tie instruction continues until any single player at the table has the highest Gold point total, so an outside player who thereby becomes the sole highest wins.
grades.observed_answer: Yes. In a double-Steal tie-break Showdown, players outside the tied pair each receive one bar from the deck. The tie rule considers the highest total anywhere at the table, so an outside player could become the winner if that bar gives them the single highest point total.
grades.reader_evidence: Double Steal: “give every other player one Gold Bar from the deck”; tied totals: repeat until “a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total.”
grades.reason: Correct conditional yes: doubleSteal compensation may give an outsider the sole highest total and tie endpoint allows any single player at the table. No missing requested part; source supports deriving this consequence from general rules.

grades.question: How does each player prepare their ID and Voting cards, what happens to cards for unused colors, and how is the initial Gold Bar pool dealt?
grades.expected_answer: Stand a visible ID in your chosen color, take the matching Voting set, remove target cards for colors not playing, and retain your Ambush card. Put the Gold deck face down and deal four central Gold Bar cards with values hidden.
grades.observed_answer: Each player chooses a color and places that color's Player ID upright in its stand in front of them. Give each player the Voting set with their color on the backs, remove cards targeting colors not in the game, and keep their own Ambush. Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center with values hidden; the deck remains face down beside the play area.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup: ‘puts its Player ID card upright in its plastic stand’; ‘Remove cards targeting colors that are not playing’; ‘Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center.’
grades.reason: Explicit upright stand and visible chosen-color ID, matching Voting cards, unused colors removed, own Ambush retained and hidden central4 deal.

grades.reason: Explicitly states no player turn order, changes until reveal, and simultaneous reveal after all have chosen.

grades.observed_answer: No four-vote majority is needed. Red is the sole Target because Red has the most votes (three); the Target is whoever receives the most votes, regardless of whether that count is a majority of all votes.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: ‘The player receiving the most votes is the Target.’
grades.reason: Applies highest count rather than absolute majority: Red alone is Target at three versus two and two.

grades.observed_answer: Red and Blue are both Targets because they tie for the most votes, and, with neither protected by a successful Ambush, both are eliminated. A player may satisfy the voting requirement and survive by voting for either tied Target.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: ‘If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets’; with tied Targets, ‘voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.’

grades.reason: Green is eliminated for voting outside the Target group despite receiving no votes.

grades.observed_answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.

grades.reason: Share/Share yields two central cards each.

grades.expected_answer: The Share player receives no bars and the Steal player receives all four.

grades.question: One finalist reveals Grab One & Go and the other Share. How are the central Gold Bars divided?
grades.expected_answer: Grab One & Go receives one bar and Share receives three.
grades.observed_answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one central bar, and the Share player receives the other three.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table: Grab One & Go against Share: ‘You get 1; opponent gets 3’; Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.
grades.reason: Grab One & Go takes one and Share three.

grades.question: Both finalists reveal Grab One & Go. How many bars does each take, how many remain central, and how many new central bars are dealt if play continues?
grades.expected_answer: Each takes one central bar. Leave the other two central and deal just two new central bars for the next round.
grades.observed_answer: Each finalist takes one central bar, leaving two in the center. If play continues, add just two new bars to the center, restoring the pool to four.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown: ‘each receives one and the other two bars remain central’; ‘Leave the remaining two in the center and add just two new bars for the next round.’
grades.reason: Each takes one; two remain and only two new central cards dealt if continuing.

grades.question: Both finalists reveal Steal. What do the finalists and the other players receive, and what happens to the central pot?
grades.expected_answer: Both finalists receive nothing. Each other player receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round rather than replacing them.
grades.observed_answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown: ‘If both choose Steal, neither finalist receives gold’; ‘give every other player one Gold Bar from the deck’; ‘Leave all four central bars for the next round.’
grades.reason: Finalists get zero, every other player one deck card; all four central cards retained without additions.

grades.question: When is victory checked, what totals win with 6–9 versus 10–12 players, and who wins if multiple players qualify with different totals?
grades.expected_answer: Check at round end after Gold Bar awards. The threshold is 25 points with 6–9 players and 24 with 10–12. When several qualify, the highest total wins.
grades.observed_answer: Check for victory at the end of the round, after Gold Bars are awarded. With 6–9 players, the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12, it is at least 24. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the player with the highest point total wins.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: ‘Check for victory at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded’; thresholds are 25 for 6–9 and 24 for 10–12; ‘the highest point total wins.’
grades.reason: Checks after awards at round end for every outcome; gives 25 for6–9,24 for10–12 and highest qualified total wins.

grades.question: At game end exactly two qualifying players tie for the highest Gold point total. What does the booklet require? If a normal round ends without a winner, which eliminated players return?
grades.expected_answer: The tied players conduct another Final Showdown, repeating until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. If no winner ends the game, every player returns next round: stand all IDs upright again.
grades.observed_answer: The booklet's instruction is that tied highest qualifying totals conduct another Final Showdown, repeating Showdowns as necessary until one player has the highest total. If a normal round has no winner, everyone returns for the next round: stand all Player ID cards upright.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: tied qualifying players ‘conduct another Final Showdown’ and ‘Repeat these Showdowns as necessary’; Turn Structure: ‘If there is no winner, everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright.’
grades.reason: Exactly two tied qualified highest players hold further Showdowns until a single highest player exists; all players return with IDs upright if normal play continues.

grades.question: Before each vote, about how long should conspiracy last, may players communicate secretly or by texting/showing cards, and who asks for final decisions when it is time to vote?
grades.expected_answer: Conspire for no longer than roughly a minute and a half. Any overt or covert means is allowed, including texting and showing Voting cards. The game owner asks players for their final decisions before voting.
grades.observed_answer: Before every vote, players discuss or signal their intended targets for roughly a minute and a half at most. Any communication method is allowed, including secretly (such as whispering), texting, or showing a Voting card. When it is time to vote, the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.
grades.reader_evidence: Conspire: ‘for roughly a minute and a half at most’; ‘Any method of communication is allowed, openly or secretly,’ including whispering, showing a Voting card, and texting; ‘the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.’
grades.reason: Gives approximate90-second maximum before each vote, any overt/covert communication including requested examples, and game-owner final-decision call.

grades.question: When casting an ordinary vote rather than Ambush, which card do you choose and where do you put it? What card replaces that choice if you suspect you are the Target?
grades.expected_answer: Choose the Voting card matching the ID color of the person you want to eliminate and place it face down in front of you. Play your own Ambush card instead of choosing another player’s card if you suspect you are the Target.
grades.observed_answer: To cast an ordinary vote, choose the Voting card matching the target's visible ID color and place it face down. If you want to defend yourself against being targeted, play your own Ambush card instead.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: ‘Each surviving player places one Voting card face down’; target with the card matching the player's visible ID color; ‘To defend yourself against being the target, play your Ambush card instead.’
grades.reason: Target-color card, face-down orientation and Ambush substitution supplied, but location in front of the voter omitted. This requested location is also omitted from the summary’s Vote prose; sourcep5 specifies it.

grades.question: After resolving a vote, how do the Player ID cards show who has been eliminated and who is eligible for the next vote?
grades.expected_answer: Knock over eliminated players’ IDs. Surviving IDs stay standing; only survivors participate in the next vote.
grades.observed_answer: Knock down the Player ID cards of eliminated players. Leave surviving players' IDs upright; they are eligible for the next vote.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: ‘Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving IDs upright for the next vote.’
grades.reason: Knocks eliminated IDs down and leaves survivors upright/eligible for next vote.

grades.question: A round awards all four central bars, either to a sole survivor or through a Showdown that distributes the entire pot. If nobody wins the game, how is the next central pool prepared?
grades.expected_answer: Deal four new central Gold Bar cards for the next round, keeping their values hidden. Refill to four only if play continues; the retained-pot exceptions apply when bars were left behind.
grades.observed_answer: If nobody wins after the round's rewards, everyone returns and all Player ID cards are stood upright. Keep central bars left behind and refill the central pool to four bars as needed; do not replace bars explicitly left there. Thus after a full-pot award leaves no bars, deal four new central bars.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: ‘Refill the central pool to four Gold Bars as needed; bars explicitly left behind remain there.’ Player Reference: ‘Keep leftover central bars and refill only to four.’
grades.reason: Refill-to4 resolves four new cards after full distribution (readerB makes number explicit). Both omit hidden-value/face-down preparation of the new pot. Independent adjudication confirms partial for that requested preparation detail.

grades.question: In the illustrated vote with four votes for Blue and three for Purple, Blue plays a successful Ambush. Does Purple become the Target because Blue survives, and may voters for Purple survive on that basis?
grades.expected_answer: No. Blue remains the Target from the tally, even though Ambush protects Blue. Purple is not promoted to Target; players who did not vote for Blue are eliminated. Blue also chooses one player who voted for Blue to eliminate.
grades.observed_answer: No. Blue remains a Target because Blue received the most votes; a successful Ambush lets Blue survive and retaliate but does not change who the vote made a Target. Purple does not become the Target on the basis of Blue surviving. Voters for Purple have not voted for a Target (Blue), so they are eliminated, unless independently protected by a successful Ambush. The summary does not give the specific Blue/Purple four-to-three example, but its stated Target and elimination rules support this result.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: most votes determines the Target and Ambush cards do not count; Ambush: it works only if its player is a Target, protects that Target, and allows one retaliation; elimination requires voting for a Target.
grades.reason: Correct fixed TargetBlue after tally and successful protection; Purple not promoted and Purple voters eliminated. Generic Ambush caveat cannot apply to ordinary Purple voters and changes no actual ruling. Blue-voter retaliation is extra key context, not requested. Independent adjudication agrees.

grades.question: Three qualifying players are tied for the highest total at game end. What tie instruction does the booklet give, and does it specify how to arrange a Final Showdown among more than two players?
grades.expected_answer: The tied players must conduct another Final Showdown until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. The booklet provides only a two-player Showdown procedure and no arrangement for three or more tied players. A specific multiway procedure is unresolved in this source; do not invent one.
grades.observed_answer: The booklet's tie instruction is to conduct another Final Showdown and repeat Showdowns as necessary until one player has the highest total. The summary says the booklet gives no arrangement or procedure for a Final Showdown involving three or more tied leaders; publisher clarification is needed.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: ‘tied players conduct another Final Showdown’ and ‘Repeat these Showdowns as necessary’; unresolved source limitation: ‘It provides no arrangement for three or more players tied.’
grades.reason: Accurately gives repeated Showdown requirement and explicitly identifies absence of a three-or-more-player arrangement; answers source-limitation question completely without inventing a solution.

grades.question: During an extra Final Showdown between two players tied for the qualifying highest total, both Steal. Could a player outside that pair become the winner if the compensation bar gives that player the single highest total?
grades.expected_answer: Yes. Double Steal gives every player outside the pair one Gold Bar from the deck while the finalists get nothing. The tie instruction continues until any single player at the table has the highest Gold point total, so an outside player who thereby becomes the sole highest wins.
grades.observed_answer: Yes, if that outside player ends the end-of-round check with a qualifying total and the single highest point total: the summary says victory is checked after bars are awarded and the highest qualifying total wins. The summary does not expressly discuss this compensation-bar tiebreak scenario, so that application is an inference from its scoring rules. If the player is not at the required threshold, the summary does not support declaring them the winner.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: victory is checked ‘at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded’; players who received bars check accumulated card point values; ‘the highest point total wins.’
grades.reason: Independent adjudicator confirms conditional yes resolves scenario. Qualifying threshold necessarily met because player becomes sole highest above the tied already-qualified pair. Inference/support partial label leaves no requested ruling unresolved.
